skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Guides the design and implementation of distinctive web interfaces through deliberate typography, color, layout, motion, copy, responsiveness, and self-critique.
skill.summary: Create subject-specific frontend designs that avoid generic visual defaults.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: The only static alert is a false positive caused by ordinary interface-writing guidance on SKILL.md line 47. The skill contains design instructions only, with no malicious intent or executable behavior.

static_findings.snippet: Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to us

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 47 discusses clear interface copy and contains no system reconnaissance instruction. The surrounding section only provides safe writing guidance for user interfaces.

content.value_statement: Generic interface patterns can make products feel interchangeable and poorly matched to their users. This skill guides intentional choices in typography, color, layout, motion, copy, and responsiveness.
actual_capabilities: Defines a subject-specific visual direction from the audience, content, and page objective.
Creates compact design tokens for color, typography, layout, and a signature element.
Uses ASCII wireframes to compare layout concepts before implementation.
Reviews design plans for generic patterns and revises weak choices.
Guides responsive implementation, keyboard focus, reduced motion, and CSS specificity.
Improves interface labels, actions, errors, empty states, and supporting copy.
limitations: Does not provide a component library, starter project, or reusable code package.
Does not replace accessibility testing, browser testing, or user research.
Requires a clear brief or permission to define the subject, audience, and page objective.
Visual quality still depends on available assets, fonts, framework constraints, and implementation tools.

use_cases.title: Launch a Product Page
use_cases.description: Create a memorable product page with a focused hero, relevant visual language, responsive behavior, and clear interface copy.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers building a new product experience

use_cases.title: Refresh an Existing Interface
use_cases.description: Replace generic visual defaults with a coherent direction while preserving the product requirements and established workflows.
use_cases.target_user: Product designers improving an existing application

use_cases.title: Define a Visual System
use_cases.description: Turn a creative brief into practical color, typography, layout, motion, and content decisions before implementation begins.
use_cases.target_user: Creative leads preparing direction for an implementation team

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Design Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a [page type] for [subject] serving [audience]. Define the page objective, palette, typography, layout concept, and one signature element.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this beginner prompt when starting from a short brief.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Responsive Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a responsive design plan for [product]. Include named colors, type roles, desktop and mobile wireframes, motion choices, and accessibility considerations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this prompt before implementing a new interface.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign a Generic Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing [page or component] against this brief: [brief]. Identify generic choices, propose specific replacements, then implement the revised direction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this prompt to reshape an existing interface.

prompt_templates.title: Lead a Full Design Critique
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as design lead for [project]. Build two directions, compare their relevance, select one, implement it, inspect screenshots, and refine weak details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this advanced prompt for iterative design and implementation.

output_examples.input: Design a homepage for a neighborhood astronomy club that needs more family memberships.
output: Direction: a field-observation journal with practical night-sky details and welcoming family photography.
Palette: Observatory Black, Paper White, Signal Red, Brass, and Twilight Blue.
Signature: an interactive observation dial that reveals upcoming viewing events.

output_examples.input: Refresh a generic analytics dashboard for an independent music distributor.
output: Replace decorative cards with dense comparison tables and focused release summaries.
Use a neutral interface palette with distinct status colors and compact utility typography.
Make release artwork and track performance the primary scanning anchors.

output_examples.input: Improve the empty state and publishing flow for an editorial tool.
output: Empty state: Create your first story to begin the issue.
Confirmation: Published to the July issue.

best_practices: Provide the real subject, audience, page objective, content, and technical constraints.
Review the design plan before implementation and explain revisions to generic choices.
Inspect desktop and mobile results, including keyboard focus, reduced motion, text fit, and CSS conflicts.
anti_patterns: Do not request a distinctive design while withholding all subject and audience context.
Do not select familiar palettes, typefaces, cards, or effects without connecting them to the brief.
Do not add motion, decoration, or copy that lacks a clear functional or thematic purpose.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a design direction, token choices, layout ideas, self-critique, implementation guidance, and interface copy suited to the brief.

faq.question: Can it redesign an existing interface?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current interface, product requirements, constraints, and the visual or usability problems that need attention.

faq.question: Does it generate frontend code?
faq.answer: It guides code implementation after the design plan is reviewed. Available output depends on the coding tools and project context.

faq.question: Does it support mobile layouts?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance requires responsive behavior down to mobile and encourages separate layout planning for smaller screens.

faq.question: Does it guarantee accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. It covers keyboard focus and reduced motion, but formal accessibility testing and standards review remain necessary.

faq.question: What information should a prompt include?
faq.answer: Include the subject, audience, page objective, real content, brand constraints, technical stack, required states, and available visual assets.
